articles.title: Amrit Him Sarovar Project Launched in Leh’s Karu, Two Water Ponds to Store 10 Million Litres - Kashmir Life
articles.full_text:
SRINAGAR: Construction of two large water-storage ponds under the Amrit Him Sarovar Project has commenced in Karu area of Leh, with a combined storage capacity of 10 million litres and the objective of strengthening water conservation and ensuring year-round availability of water in the region.
The project envisages diverting water from the perennial Karu Nallah through newly constructed channels to feed the two ponds, which will cater to the water requirements of a 225-acre area on both sides of the stream, according to the project details shared by the authorities.
Each pond will measure 60 metres in length, 40 metres in width and two metres in depth, with an individual storage capacity of five million litres.
Work on the project commenced on November 10, 2026, and is scheduled for completion by January 15, 2027.
The project will utilise the seasonal and perennial flow of Karu Nallah, which has a reported peak summer discharge of 350 million litres per day, equivalent to 150 cusecs, while maintaining a winter flow of around 170 million litres per day despite sub-zero temperatures.
The proposed water-storage infrastructure is expected to serve 225 acres of land, including 65 acres (25 hectares) on the right bank and 160 acres (65 hectares) on the left bank of the stream.
The initiative is aimed at improving water conservation, enabling better utilisation of available water resources throughout the year and creating opportunities for expanding agricultural activities in the region.
The project is being undertaken in line with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of strengthening water conservation and ensuring long-term water security.
Beyond creating storage infrastructure, the initiative is intended to support agricultural development, promote sustainable use of water resources and benefit local communities in Ladakh.
